scope: Feature branch 029-people-organizations-api vs origin/main (fairdm/, docs/, tests/, specs/011-restful-api/spec.md), one pass through four lenses: security and privacy, correctness, spec compliance, documentation. tests/test_api ran green (1306 passed). 139 new or changed tests swept; 22 mutations applied and restored, of which 4 left the suite green (2 of those are findings, 2 are harmless).

findings.claim: ADR 0027 now describes a credit wrongly. It says a credit names its contributor and affiliation as {"uuid", "url"} references through RecordReferenceField, and that a reference to someone the caller may not see is null. The branch replaced that shape and did not touch the ADR.
findings.evidence: docs/adr/0027-records-refer-to-each-other-by-short-identifier.md:9-10 ('a credit its contributor and affiliation' in the list of things returned as {"uuid": ..., "url": ...}) and :15 ('One field class, RecordReferenceField, does this for every relation'). fairdm/api/serializers.py:526-609: ContributionSerializer has no RecordReferenceField; uuid and url are flat keys beside name, name_type, given_name, family_name and name_identifiers, and affiliation is a list of {uuid, url, name, affiliation_identifier, affiliation_identifier_scheme, scheme_uri}. A credit held by a superuser is returned with its name and identifiers (serializers.py:563-577), which the ADR's 'a reference never names a record the caller may not see' no longer covers. `git diff origin/main...HEAD --stat -- docs/adr` lists 0029, 0030 and index.md only. ADR 0030 and restful-api.md describe the new shape correctly.
findings.suggested_fix: In ADR 0027 take 'and a credit its contributor and affiliation' out of the list of references, and add one sentence saying a credit is not a reference and is described in ADR 0030. Leave the rest of the ADR, which still holds for project, dataset, sample and owner.

findings.claim: The test that an affiliation gives its ROR ID when the organization holds two identifiers cannot fail. The ROR ID is created first, so 'the first identifier held' and 'the ROR ID' are the same row.
findings.evidence: tests/test_api/test_viewsets.py:753-765 test_an_affiliation_with_two_identifiers_gives_its_ror_id: the `author` fixture (lines 519-533) creates the ROR identifier, then the test adds a Wikidata one, so ROR has the lower pk. fairdm/api/serializers.py:480-481 sorts by pk and prefers ROR. Mutation run: replacing line 481 with `return held[0] if held else None` leaves all 1306 tests in tests/test_api green. The documented rule in docs/portal-development/restful-api.md ('The organization's ROR ID where it has one, and otherwise its first identifier') therefore has no test that reads it.
findings.reproduction: Replace serializers.py:481 with `return held[0] if held else None`; run `uv run pytest -q -n0 tests/test_api`; 1306 passed.
findings.suggested_fix: In that test create the Wikidata identifier before the ROR one (build the organization in the test, not from the `author` fixture), and assert affiliation_identifier is the ROR address. The repaired test must fail under the mutation `return held[0] if held else None`.

findings.claim: A credit for a person with no given or family name returns given_name and family_name as empty strings, not null. A script filling a DataCite creator from the credit writes an empty givenName and familyName.
findings.evidence: fairdm/api/serializers.py:591-599 return credit.given_name / credit.family_name as stored; Person.first_name and last_name are blank strings, not null. Probe on the branch, public dataset credited to PersonFactory(first_name='', last_name='', name='Mononym'): GET /api/v1/datasets/{uuid}/ returned {"name": "Mononym", "name_type": "Personal", "given_name": "", "family_name": ""}. The same holds on the list. get_name already treats empty as absent (serializers.py:584). The schema types both as nullable strings and the docs say only that both are null for an organization.
findings.suggested_fix: Return `credit.given_name or None` and `credit.family_name or None` for a person in get_given_name and get_family_name.

findings.claim: No test reads the default order of the people or the organizations list. The default can change from name to anything stable and the suite stays green.
findings.evidence: fairdm/api/viewsets.py:210 and :240-242 order by (name, pk). Mutation run: changing the people queryset to `.order_by("pk")` leaves all 1306 tests in tests/test_api green. The sorting tests (test_viewsets.py:1438, :1902) always send ?ordering=.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one test per list that creates three entries whose names are out of creation order and asserts the names come back sorted with no ?ordering sent. It must fail under the mutation `.order_by("pk")`.

findings.claim: The people list can be ordered by `modified` and narrowed with modified_after and modified_before, and a person's `modified` moves on every full save of their row, including saves that change only account fields. A caller can therefore learn when a person's account row last changed, although the value itself is never returned.
findings.evidence: fairdm/contrib/contributors/models.py:200-205 `modified = DateTimeField(auto_now=True)` on Contributor, which Person shares with its account fields. fairdm/api/viewsets.py:194 lists `modified` and `added` in PersonViewSet.ordering_fields, and ChangedSinceFilterSet (fairdm/api/filters.py:237-255) is added to every list. A sign-in does not move it (Django saves last_login with update_fields). A password or email change that calls a plain save() does; I did not trace which account flows call a full save, which is why this is `likely`. Spec FR-021 says no response may carry an account detail; this is inference from a filter, and FR-004 asks for the changed-since filters on both lists, so the two requirements meet here.
findings.suggested_fix: No code change is needed to merge. Tell the maintainer at the merge gate, beside the two points decisions.md D9 already raises, so the trade-off is accepted knowingly or `modified` is dropped from the people list's ordering and filters.

notes: docs/portal-development/restful-api.md and docs/user-guide/reading-records-with-a-script.md: the example identifiers for a person start with 'p' (pXq7Lw0e...) and for an organization with 'o' (oT5mYh1u...). Every person and organization identifier starts with 'c' (Contributor.uuid prefix), and 'p' is what a project's starts with. The credit example in the same page uses 'c' correctly.

docs/portal-development/restful-api.md 'Filtering organizations': an unknown value for ?type= is answered 400 (ChoiceFilter). decisions.md D17 records this; the page does not say it, while it does say so for ?parent= and ?organization=.

docs/portal-development/restful-api.md: country codes are matched exactly, so ?country=au finds nothing. The page says 'in capitals', which covers it; the user guide page says only 'a two-letter code'.

fairdm/api/filters.py:80-82: the FairDMVisibilityFilter docstring still says models with no visibility mechanism 'such as Contributor' are fully public; the people viewset now leaves accounts out in its own queryset.

RecordReferenceField.route_name (serializers.py:206-209) sends any contributor that is not an organization to api:person-detail, including a bare Contributor row with no concrete type. No current path creates one.
Removing the 'sub_organizations' prefetch from OrganizationViewSet leaves the suite green. It is one query either way for a single record, so nothing is lost.

Members of an organization are filtered twice, in the viewset's prefetch and in OrganizationSerializer.get_members. Removing either alone leaves the suite green and removing both fails two tests, so the behaviour is covered and the serializer's own guard is not covered on its own.

Security pass, nothing found: with a superuser, the anonymous account, a pending member and an ended member all affiliated to one organization, the organization's record listed only the verified current member, ?organization= on the people list returned only that member, and ?email=, ?is_superuser=, ?is_staff=, ?search= and ?ordering=email on the people list changed nothing. The generated schema has no component carrying email, password, is_staff, is_superuser, is_active, last_login, date_joined, groups, user_permissions, is_claimed, level, id or pk, and no path under /contributors/.
The contributor filter on projects and datasets held under mutation: dropping get_visible(), dropping real() from the person lookup, and switching to get_public_projects() each turned a test red.

Query-count tests can fail: removing the people prefetch, the organizations prefetch, the credit roles prefetch, the credit affiliation-identifier prefetch and the members' select_related each turned the matching test red. They compare 2 records against 12, and 1 credited person against 3.

FR and SC coverage: every FR-001 to FR-024 and SC-001 to SC-006 has a test that reads the requirement, apart from the two gaps in TEST-001 and TEST-002. FR-025 and SC-007 are read by tests/test_api/test_schema.py (exact key sets for a credit, a person, an affiliation, an organization and a member, and the filter parameters). FR-026 and FR-027 are documentation and have no test, which the testing standard allows.
Deactivated people (is_active false) are listed and served, as on the portal's own people list and person page, which use the same Person.objects.real().
